Char: Reason for exclusion: Ineligible comparison group. Quasi-cluster randomised trial in Botswana. Schools with children, aged 5-11 years, were assigned to a 1) micronutrient fortified beverage (β-carotene 2400 µg, riboflavin 0.4 mg, niacin 2.7 mg, pyridoxine 0.5 mg, folic acid 140 µg, cyanocobalamin 1 µg, ascorbic acid 60 mg, dl-α-tocopherol 7.5 mg, tricalcium phosphate 120 mg, ferrous bisyglycinate chelate 7 mg, potassium iodide 60 µg, zinc gluconate 3.75 mg), or 2) non-fortified beverage (isoenergetic placebo drink; same beverage without micronutrients).

Ineligible comparison group. Cluster randomised trial with a mixed methods approach in Bangladesh. Schools with children, aged 6-11 years, were randomly assigned a 1) fortified biscuit (multiple micronutrients with vitamin B12) or 2) no biscuit (no intervention).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Ghana. Infants, 5 months of age, were randomly assigned to 1) sprinkles powder (β-carotene 300 μg RE, vitamin C 50 mg, vitamin D3 7.5 μg, folic acid 150 μg, iron 12.5 mg, zinc 5 mg), 2) crushable Nutritabs tablets (multiple micronutrients with vitamin B12 0.5 μg), or 3) energy-dense Nutributter (multiple micronutrients with vitamin B12 0.5 μg).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised double-blind controlled trial in Bangladesh. Girls, aged 11–17 years, were assigned to 1) multiple micronutrients once-weekly (vitamin A 1600 mg,  vitamin D 10 mg, vitamin E 20 mg, vitamin C 140 mg, vitamin B1 2.8mg, vitamin B2 2.8 mg, niacin 36 mg, vitamin B6 3.8 mg, vitamin B12 5.2 mg, folic acid 400 mg, iron 60 mg, zinc 30 mg, copper 4 mg, selenium 130 mg, iodine 300 mg), 2) same multiple micronutrients twice-weekly or 3) iron and folic acid (60 mg iron and 400 μg folic acid).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Palestine. Infants, 6 months of age, were randomly assigned to 1) micronutrient powder (vitamin A 400 μg, vitamin C 30 mg, vitamin D 5 μg, vitamin E 5 mg, α-TE Vitamin B1 0.5 mg, vitamin B2 0.5 mg, vitamin B6 0.5 mg, vitamin B12 0.9 μg, folic acid 90 μg, niacin 6 mg, iron (fumarate) 10 mg, zinc 4.1 mg, copper 0.56 mg, selenium 17 μg, and Iodine 90 μg) plus National Micronutrient Supplement (NMS) (vitamin A 300–600 μg, vitamin D 10 μg, iron sulphate 2 mg/kg), or 2) NMS alone.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Mexico. Children, 6-12 months, were randomly assigned to a 1) milk-based fortified food (sodium 24.5 mg, Iron 10 mg, Zinc 10 mg, Vitamin A 400 μg, Vitamin E 6 mg, Vitamin C 50 mg, Vitamin B2 0.8 mg, Vitamin B12 0.7 μg, Folic acid 50 μg), 2) micronutrient powders (Iron (mg ) 10.0, Zinc 10 mg, Vitamin A 400 μg, Vitamin E 6 mg, Vitamin C 50 mg, Vitamin B2 0.8 mg, Vitamin B12 0.7 μg, Folic acid 50 μg), or 3) micronutrient syrup (Iron 10 mg, Zinc 10 mg, Vitamin A 400 μg, Vitamin E 6 mg, Vitamin C 50 mg, Vitamin B2 0.8 mg, Vitamin B12 0.7 μg, Folic acid 50.0 μg).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised, double-blind placebo-controlled trial in Tanzania. Children, aged 6-11 years, were randomly assigned to a 1) fortified beverage (ferrous glycinate 5.4 mg, Vitamin A retinyl palmitate 526 µg RE, Iodine 45 µg, Vitamin B2 0.6 mg, Vitamin B6 0.7 mg, Vitamin B12 3 µg, Folic acid 140 µg, Zinc 5.25 mg, Vitamin C 72 mg), or 2) non-fortified beverage (isoenergetic placebo drink; same beverage without micronutrients).

Ineligible route of administration (injection). Double-blind randomised controlled trial in Norway. Infants, aged less than 8 months, were randomly assigned  to receive 1) intramuscular vitamin B12 (400 µg) or 2) no intervention.

Ineligible comparison group. Cluster-randomised controlled trial in India. Preschools with children, aged 29-49 months, were randomly assigned to 1) multiple micronutrient powder (Iron, Vitamin A, Vitamin C, Folic Acid, Zinc, Vitamin B12, Vitamin B2) or 2) a placebo.

Ineligibile comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Wales. Schools with children, aged 11-13 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a vitamin and mineral supplement (pionavanoids 50 mg; biotin 100 μg; choline bitartrate 70 mg; folic acid 100 μg; inositol 30 mg; niacin 50 mg; pantothenic acid 50 mg; para-aminobenzoic acid 10 mg; vitamin B6 12 mg; vitamin B1 3-9 mg; vitamin B2 5 mg; vitamin A 375 μg; vitamin B12 10 μg; vitamin C 500 mg; vitamin D3 g; vitamin E 70 IU; vitamin K 100 μg, Calcium gluconate 100 mg; chromium 0-2 mg; magnesium 7-6 mg; manganese 1-5 mg; molybdenum 0-1 mg; iodine 50 μg; iron 1-3 3 mg; zinc 10 mg) or 2) a placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Clinical trial registry of a randomised controlled trial in India. Children, aged 6-11 years, will be randomly assigned to 1) a protein product (8g legume based protein product) with micronutrients , 2) a protein product (8 g legume based protein product) without micronutrients , or 3) no intervention.

Ineligible comparison group. Clinical trial registry of a randomised controlled trial in India. Children, aged 6-12 years, will be randomly assigned to 1) rice fortified with micronutrients (iron 4.25 mg per 100 g, vitamin B12 0.125 µg  per 100 g, folic acid: 12.50 µg  per 100g), or 2) non-fortified  rice.

Ineligible comparison group. Clinical trial registry of a randomised trial in India. Children, aged 12-59 mo, will be randomly assigned 1) fortified salt (1.34 mg of iron, 1.4 mg of zinc,  0.6μg of vitamin B12, 52.4 μg folic acid, 30 μg of iodine; all per gram of salt), or 2) iodized salt (30 μg of iodine per gram of salt).

Ineligible comparison group. Quasi-randomised controlled trial in Russia. Children, aged 8-10 years, were assigned 1) 1.5 g of orotic acid, 60 mg of folic acid, plus 10 µg of vitamin B12 or 2) the standard treatment (not defined by study authors).

Ineligible route of administration (injection). Quasi-randomised controlled trial in Russia. Children, aged 6 months to 15 years, with haemolytic anaemia, assigned to 1) intramuscular vitamin B12 100 µg  or 2) no intervention.

Ineligible comparison group. Quasi-randomised trial in the United States of America. Premature infants, in 1 week of life, were assigned to 1) 0.6 cc polyvisol, and aqueous polyvitamin preparation, containing vitamin B12, or 2) 0.6 cc polyvisol and 30 µg of vitamin B12 until discharge.

Ineligible comparison group. Secondary analysis of a randomised controlled trial in Burkina Faso. Children, aged 6 to 23 months, with moderate acute malnutrition were randomly assigned to 1) lipid-based nutrient supplement with vitamin B12 0.9 µg  or 2) a corn-soy blend with vitamin B12 0.9 µg, each with either dehulled soy or soy isolate, and milk protein (0%, 20%, or 50%). Ineligible comparison group. Protocol for a randomised controlled trial in Guatemala. Children, aged 6–24 months, will be randomly assigned to 1) a programme behavioural change strategy and small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (Energy 118 kcal, Proteins 2.6 g, Lipids 9.6 g, Calcium 280 mg, Linoleic acid 2.81 g, α-linolenic acid 0.58 g, Phosphorous 190 mg, Potassium 200 mg, Magnesium 40 mg, Zinc 8 mg, Copper 0.34 mg, Iron 9 mg, Iodine 90 µg, Selenium 20 µg, Manganese 1.2 µg, Vitamin B1 0.3 mg, Vitamin B2 0.4 mg, Niacin 4.0 mg, Pantothenic acid 1.8 mg, Vitamin B6 0.3 mg, Folic acid 80 µg, Vitamin B12 0.5 µg, Vitamin C 30 mg, Vitamin D 5 µg, Vitamin E 6.0 mg, Vitamin K 30 µg, and Sodium 20 mg), 2) programme behavioural change strategy and micronutrient powders (15-micronutrient formulation with vitamin B12) or 3) micronutrient powders with vitamin B12 only.

Ineligible intervention group. Randomised controlled trial in Kenya. Children, aged 6-9 years, were randomly assigned to 1) an energy supplement (githeri), 2) a milk supplement (githeri plus a 200 mL of milk), 3) a meat supplement (githeri with 60 g minced beef), or 4) no food supplement.

Ineligible route of administration (intravenous and subcutaneous). Randomised controlled trial in Austria. Premature infants, weighing 801-1300 g, were randomly assigned to receive 1) intravenous vitamin B12 (3 μg/kg/day), subcutaneous vitamin B12 (21 μg/kg/week) and oral folic acid (100 μg/kg/day), or 2) oral folic acid (60 μg/kg/day), both groups received iron, vitamin E and erythropoietin.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in the United Kingdom. Children, aged 8-14 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a multi-vitamin/mineral supplement (L-Lysine monohydrochloride 50 mg,  β-Carotene 0.514 mg, Vitamin A 715 IU,  Thiamine nitrate 0.5 mg, Vitamin B2 0.55 mg, Pyridoxine hydrochloride 0.55 mg, Vitamin B12 0.600 mg, Vitamin C 22 mg, Vitamin D3 150 IU, Vitamin E 5.215 mg, Folic acid 50 mg, Biotin 15.00mg , Nicotinamide 6.00 mg, Copper (II) 0.3 mg, Calcium phosphate 65 mg, Ferrous (II) fumarate 2.5 mg, Zinc oxide 2.5 mg and Magnesium oxide 12.5 mg)  or 2) a placebo .

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Lao People's Democratic Republic. Children, aged 6-23 months, were randomly assigned 1) micronutrient powder (6 mg iron, 10 mg zinc and thirteen other micronutrients), or 2) a placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Cluster-randomised trial in Cambodia. Infants, aged 6 months, were randomly assigned to 1) micronutrient sprinkles (14 micronutirents including vitamin B12 0.9 μg) and infant and young child feeding (IYCF) education or 2) IYCF only.

Ineligible route of administration (intramuscular). Clinical trial in France. Premature infants, with blood reticulocytosis is below 45,000/mm3, were assigned an intramuscular injection of calcium folinate (5 mg) and vitamin B12 (1000 µg).

Ineligible comparison group. Cluster-randomised placebo-controlled trial in Cambodia. Sixteen schools with children, aged 6-16 years, were randomly assigned to four groups either receiving one of three extruded-fortified rice (each containing Iron, Zinc, Vitamin B1, Folic Acid, Vitamin A, Vitamin B3, Vitamin B12 and Vitamin B6) or placebo (unfortified rice).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in the United States. Children, aged 6-17 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a controlled diet with vitamin B12 (20μg), or 2) controlled diet with placebo. Both groups received a daily multiple vitamin supplement containing vitamin 1 μg B12 activity.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised, double‐blind, placebo‐controlled trial in Tanzania. Infants, at 6 weeks of age, were randomly assigned to 1) zinc only (5mg zinc sulfate) 2), zinc and multivitamin supplementation (5mg zinc sulfate, 60 mg of vitamin C, 8 mg of vitamin E, 0.5 mg of vitamin B1, 0.6 mg of vitamin B2, 4 mg of niacin, 0.6 mg of B6, 130μg of folic acid and 1μg of vitamin B12),  3) multivitamin supplementation only (60 mg of vitamin C, 8 mg of vitamin E, 0.5 mg of vitamin B1, 0.6 mg of vitamin B2, 4 mg of niacin, 0.6 mg of B6, 130μg of folic acid and 1μg of vitamin B12), or 4) a placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Australia and New Zealand. Children, aged 12-23 months, were randomly assigned 1) a reduced protein, micronutrient-fortified milk (including iron, vitamin D3, vitamin B12, and vitamin C) or 2) plain cow's milk .

Ineligible route of administration (intramuscular). Randomised double-blind controlled trial in Chile. Preterm newborns (< 34 weeks and < 1.850 g) were randomly assigned  to 1) intramuscular vitamin B12 (100 mg) or 2) a placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial in Zambia. Children, aged 7-15 years, were randomly assigned 1) iron supplementation (60 mg elemental iron), 2) iron and multi-micronutrient supplementation (60 mg elemental iron, vitamin A 2000 g, vitamin B1 2.6 mg, vitamin B2 3 mg, vitamin B6 3.4 mg, vitamin B12 4g, vitamin C 100 mg, vitamin D 20g, vitamin E 20 mg, niacin 34 mg, folate 300g, zinc 30 mg, iodine 300 g, copper 4 mg and selenium 80 g), 3) multi-micronutrient supplementation  (vitamin A 2000 g, vitamin B1 2.6 mg, vitamin B2 3 mg, vitamin B6 3.4 mg, vitamin B12 4g, vitamin C 100 mg, vitamin D 20g, vitamin E 20 mg, niacin 34 mg, folate 300g, zinc 30 mg, iodine 300 g, copper 4 mg and selenium 80 g), or 4) placebo.

Ineligible route of administration (intramuscular). Clinical trials registry of a randomised crossover controlled trial in the United States. Children, aged 3-7 years, with autistic disorder were randomly assigned to 1) a nutritional supplement (carnitine (250 mg), magnesium citrate (200 mg), selenium (50 µg); zinc picolinate (25 mg), molybdenum (50 µg), calcium citrate (400 mg), cod liver oil (1/2 teaspoon), vitamin C (500 mg), vitamin B1 (3 mg), vitamin B2 (3.4 mg), vitamin B352 (20 mg), vitamin B6 (4 mg) pantothenic acid(10 mg), biotin (300 µg), pyridoxal (25mg), folinic acid (800 µg), and vitamin B12 (75 μg/kg every 3 days)), or 2) placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Clinical trials registry of a randomised controlled trial in Bangladesh. Children, aged 8-10 years, exposed to arsenic in their drinking water, were randomly assigned to 1)  folic acid 400μg plus vitamin B12 5 μg, or 2) a placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Clinical trials registry of a randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial in China. Children, aged 6 months to 2 years, will be randomly assigned 1) vitamin B12 (1.2 μg) and folic acid (0.4 mg), or 2) a placebo 3 days before surgery.

Ineligible route of administration (intramuscular). Quasi-randomised controlled trial in Italy. Children, aged 3-12 years, were allocated to one of five groups, 1) anabolic steroid (100 µg/kg/day) plus cobamamide (100 µg/kg/day), 2) anabolic steroid (50 µg/kg/day) plus cobamamide (100 µg/kg/day), 3) anabolic steroid alone (100 µg/kg/day), 4) cobamamide alone (100 µg/kg/day) or 5) placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised, placebo-controlled trial in Australia and Indonesia. Children, aged 6-10 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a micronutrient mix drink (iron, folate, vitamin A, vitamin C, vitamin B6, and vitamin B12 at one times the Recommended Dietary Allowance (RDA) or Recommended Daily Intake (RDI) and zinc at one-half the RDA/RDI ) 2) docosahexanoic acid (DHA) and eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA) (88 mg DHA and 22 mg EPA), 3) group 1 and group 2 or 4) placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Community-based randomised double-blind trial in Burkina Faso. Children, aged 6-23 months, with anemia were randomly assigned to 1) iron 15 mg, 2) iron 15 mg plus zinc 10 mg, or 3) multiple micronutrients (15 mg iron, 10 mg zinc, 375 μg vitamin A, 5 μg vitamin D, 6 mg vitamin E, 0.5 mg vitamin B1, 0.5 mg riboflavin, 6 mg niacin, 150 μg folic acid, 0.5 mg vitamin B6, 0.9 mg vitamin B12, 35 mg vitamin C, 10 μg vitamin K, 50 μg iodine, and 0.7 mg copper).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised open-label dose response trial in Nigeria. Toddlers, aged 1-3 years, with mild-moderate andmeia and malnutrition were randomly assigned 1) 200mL of a multi-nutrient fortified dairy-based drink (Protein, Carbohydrates, Sucrose, Lactose, Fat, DHA, Calcium, Phosphorus, Potassium, Magnesium, Sodium, Iron, Copper, Zinc, Iodine, Selenium, Vitamin A, Vitamin D3, Vitamin E, Vitamin B1, Vitamin B2, Vitamin B6, Folic acid, Vitamin B12, Vitamin K1, Biotin, Niacin, and Pantothenic acid), 2) 400 mL of same multi-nutrient fortified dairy-based drink, or 3) 600 mL of same multi-nutrient fortified dairy-based drink daily for 6 months.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Spain. Children, aged 8-14 years, were randomly assigned  to 1) milk fortified with micronutrients (vitamin A, vitamin B1, vitamin B2, vitamin B3, pantothenic acid, vitamin B6, biotin, folic acid, vitamin B12, vitamin C, vitamin D, vitamin E, calcium, phosphorus, and zinc) and poly-unsaturated fatty acids (DHA), eicosapentaenoic acid (EPA), and oleic acid) or 2) non-fortified milk.

Ineligible comparison group. Quasi-randomised controlled trial in Germany. Children, with hypochromic anemia, were assigned 1) iron plus vitamin supplements (104.4 mg iron, folic acid, riboflavin, vitamins C, B6 and B12), or 2) iron alone (104.4 mg iron) and were compared to hematologically healthy controls.

Ineligible comparison group. Quasi-randomised controlled trial in Italy. Children, aged 1 month to 3 years, with underweight, anorexia, and dystrophy were assigned to 1) dimethazine (0.05 mg/kg), 2) cobamamide (3.00 mg), or 3) dimethazine (0.05 mg/kg) and cobamamide (3 mg).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised double-blind clinical trial in Mexico. Children, 12-30 months, were randomly assigned to 1) milk-based formula with micronutrients including vitamin B12 1.65 µg, and poly-unsaturated fatty acids (linoleic acid, alpha-linolenic acid , and docosahexaenoic acid , or 2) milk-based formula with micronutrients only (without vitamin B12).

Ineligible comparison group. Quasi-experimental study in Ethiopia. Children, aged 6-23 months, were allocated to 1) micronutrient powder (vitamin A 1332 IU/400 µg, vitamin D 200 IU/5 µg, vitamin E 5 mg TE, vitamin B1 0.5 mg, vitamin B2 0.5 mg, vitamin B6 0.5 mg, vitamin B12 0.9 µg, niacinamide 6 mg, folate 150 µg, vitamin C 30 mg, iron 6mg, zinc 4.1 mg, copper 0.56 mg, selenium 17 µg, and iodine 90 µg), or 2) placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in India. Boys, aged 5-11 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a B-complex vitamin supplement (thiamin 1 mg, riboflavin 1.5 mg, pyridoxine 1.5 mg, niacin 15 mg, folic acid 0.1 mg and vitamin B12 0.001mg), or 2) a placebo (100 mg lactose).

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Japan. Children, aged 10-11 years, were randomly assigned to 1)  L-lysine hydrochloride 0.9 g plus a vitamin mixture (6 mg of vitamin B1, 6 mg of vitamin B2, 3 mg of vitamin B6, and 15 γ of vitamin B12), 2) vitamin mixture alone or, 3) no intervention.
Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in Italy. Children, aged 6-12 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a multi-vitamin supplement (Vitality Roeder 2000 Junior), or 2) a placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in the United States. Children, aged 6-12 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a vitamin-mineral supplement (containing 50% to 67% RDA for 11 vitamins and 7 minerals including vitamin B12), or 2) a placebo daily for 3 months.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised placebo-controlled intervention trial in Cambodia. Infants, aged 6-24 months, received either 1) iron plus folic acid (IFA) (30 mg ferrous sulfate, and 300 μg folic acid), 2) IFA plus a micronutrient (30 mg ferrous sulfate, 300 μg folic acid, 375 RAE vitamin A, 10 μg vitamin D, 12 mg vitamin E (α-tocopherol equivalents), 1 mg vitamin B1, 1 mg vitamin B6, 12 mg niacin, 1.8 μg vitamin B12, 70 mg vitamin C, 10 mg zinc, 1.2 mg copper, 40 μg selenium and 100 μg  iodine), or 2) placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in India. Children, aged 6-60 months, were randomly assigned to 1) 2 μg vitamin B12 and 250 μg folic acid, 2) 5 mg iron, 2 μg vitamin B12 and 250 μg folic acid 3) 10mg iron, 2 μg vitamin B12 and 250 μg folic acid, 4) 20 mg iron, 2 μg vitamin B12 and 250 μg folic acid, or 5) 40 mg iron, 2 μg vitamin B12 and 250 μg folic acid.

Ineligible comparison group. Double-blind randomised controlled trial in India. Children, aged 6-18 years, were randomly assigned to 1) a micronutrient-enriched beverage (containing 100% RDA for iron, riboflavin (B2), pyridoxine (B6), vitamin B12, folate, and vitamin C; 50% RDA for vitamins A, D, and B1, niacin, calcium, and iodine; and 15% RDA for zinc) or 2) placebo, daily for 14 months.

Ineligible comparison group. Double-blind randomised placebo-controlled trial in South Africa, Peru, Vietnam, and Indonesia. Infants, aged 6-11 months, were randomly to receive 1) multiple-micronutrient supplement (2 RDAs of vitamins A, D, E, C, B1, B2, B6, B12, niacin, folic acid, iron, zinc, copper, and iodine) weekly, 2) multiple-micronutrient supplement (1 RDA of vitamins A, D, E, C, B1, B2, B6, B12, niacin, folic acid, iron, zinc, copper, and iodine) daily, 3) iron supplement (10mg) daily, or 4) placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised controlled trial in South Africa. Infants, aged 6-12 months, were randomly assigned to receive 1) small-quantity lipid-based nutrient supplements (SQ-LNS) (linoleic acid, α-linolenic acid, plus 20 micronutrients), 2) SQ-LNS plus (linoleic acid, α-linolenic acid, docosahexaenoic acid, arachidonic acid plus 26 micronutrients), or 3) a placebo.

Ineligible route of administration (intramuscular). Randomised controlled trial in China. Children, aged 6 months to 6 years, with cerebral palsy were randomly assigned  to 1) vitamin B12 25μg (orally and intramuscularly) and mouse nerve growth factor (18 μg), or 2) mouse nerve growth factor (18 μg) alone.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised double-blind placebo-controlled trial in India. Children, aged 6-12 years, with low serum ferritin (SF < 20 μg/L) were randomly assigned to 1) a multiple micronutrient fortified drink (containing 20 to 70% of the RDA for vitamin A, B2, B12, C, folic acid, iron and zinc), or 2) a placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised double-blind controlled trial in India. Children, aged 6-10 years, were randomly assigned to 1) high dose miconutrients (100% RDA of iodine, iron, vitamin B2, vitamin B6, vitamin B12, folate, zinc, calcium, vitamin A and vitamin C) with high dose α-linolenic acid (ALA) (900 mg ALA) plus  docosahexaenoic acid (100 mg DHA), 2) high dose micronutrients with low dose of ALA 140 mg, 3) low dose micronutrients (15% RDA for  iodine, iron, vitamin B2, vitamin B6, vitamin B12, folate, zinc, calcium, vitamin A and vitamin C) with high dose ALA, or 4) low dose micronutrients and low dose of ALA.

Ineligible route of administration (intramuscular). Double-blind randomised controlled trial in Norway. Healthy infants, birthweight 2000-3000 g, with impaired total homocysteine (tHcy  >  6.5 μmol/L) were randomly assigned 1) 400 μg hydroxycobalamin intramuscularly, or 2) a placebo injection.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised community-based controlled trial in Guinea-Bissau. Children, under 3 years, with persistent diarrhea were randomly assigned to 1) millet gruel with a micronutrient supplement (2 RDAs of vitamin A, thiamine, riboflavin, vitamin B6, vitamin B12, folic acid, niacin, pantothenic acid, vitamin C, vitamin D, vitamin E, iron, zinc, copper, iodine, and selenium), or 2) no dietary treatment/intervention.

Ineligible comparison group. Randomised trial in Tanzania. Children, aged 6-60 months, were randomly assigned to 1) zinc gluconate 10 mg, 2) zinc gluconate 10 mg with micronutrients (ferrous fumarate 18 mg, folic acid 93.75 mg, vitamin A (450 mg, as retinyl palmitate), vitamin B12 1.17 mg, vitamin B1 (0.625 mg as thiamine nitrate), vitamin B2 0.55 mg, copper 340 mg, and vitamin E (6.6 mg as RRR-atocopherol)), 3) micronutrient supplementation (ferrous fumarate 18 mg, folic acid 93.75 mg, retinyl palmitate 450 mg, vitamin B12 1.17 mg, thiamine nitrate 0.625 mg, vitamin B2 0.55 mg, copper 340 mg, and vitamin E (6.6 mg as RRR-α tocopherol)), or 4) placebo.

Ineligible comparison group. Quasi-randomised clinical trial in China. Preterm infants were assigned to 1) a parenteral nutrition injection (containing 40 µg/ml folic acid, 0.5 µg/ml vitamin B12) plus fortified powdered milk (containing 40 µg/100 ml, folic acid , 0.5 µg/100 ml vitamin B12, 1 mg/100 ml iron) , or 2) the same intervention plus 200 µg/kg folic acid  and 30 µg/kg vitamin B12.

Ineligible route of administration (intramuscular). Randomised trial in the United States. Premature infants, less than 1800g and less than 36 weeks gestation, were randomly assigned 1) intramuscular vitamin B12 100 μg, monthly, 2) oral folate 0.1mg, daily, 2) intramuscular vitamin B12 100μg, monthly plus oral folate 0.1mg, daily,  or 4) no intervention.
